title: Curated honour
description: One row of data/curated/honours.jsonl: a distinction the source states for one player at one admitted tournament (`IndividualAchievements`), such as a Worlds finals MVP or an All-Pro team place. A distinction is a fact about (player, event), so it is its own record rather than a field on either entity. The title and the award type travel verbatim: the source states one type (`Season Award`) for every award, and names the distinction in free text, so the dataset does not pretend to a controlled vocabulary. Contains no build timestamp, so the file is byte-identical across builds (spec R8).

id.description: Opaque surrogate key derived from the source tuple that identifies the row (event page, player page, title and the page the award was stated on), so a re-crawl cannot renumber it (spec D3). Do not parse it: read the row through `title` and `playerName`.

eventId.description: The admitted event the award belongs to. The award's own page may be a stage sub-page of that event (`2024 Season World Championship/Main Event`); the record keeps the event it belongs to, so an award never floats free of the corpus's event list.

eventName.description: The event's display name, so the row reads without a join (spec R12).

playerId.description: The player the distinction belongs to. A player named only by an award (a coach, an analyst) is still a player the corpus references, so the entity is emitted in players.jsonl even when no player-game row names them.

playerName.description: The player's current handle, so the row reads without a join.

sourcePlayer.description: The source's own `Player` string, verbatim, so the row walks back to the award table (spec R7). It is a page name or one of its aliases, never the identity.

team.description: The source's `Team` string, verbatim. Absent when the source states none. A team string the registry does not resolve is carried and no entity is minted from it: an award is context, not evidence that a team existed.

teamId.description: The team the corpus knows, when the alias registry resolves the stated string (`SKT T1` -> `T1`). Absent when it does not: the string stays on `team` and the distinction is still emitted.

teamName.description: That team's current display name, so a resolved team reads without a join.

title.description: The distinction as the source words it (`Finals MVP`, `Most Valuable Player`, `All Pro Team`). Never normalised: the corpus keeps the three spellings of the same idea distinct, because deciding they are one is the analyst's judgement, not the build's.

type.description: The source's `AchievementType`, verbatim. One value today (`Season Award`) for tournament MVPs and regional season awards alike, which is why the title, not this field, names the distinction.

sourcePage.description: The page the award was stated on, for provenance: the event's own page or a stage sub-page of it.

place.description: The source's `Place` text when it states one. Absent when the source states none, which is the case for every recorded row so far: the MVP rows state no place, and neither do the All-Pro rows, whose rank lives in the title (`3rd All Pro Team`) rather than here.

placeNumber.description: The source's `Place_Number` when it states one. Absent when it states none: a stated place of `1` is 1, and no place is not 0.
